title: Cretaceous Intrusive Rocks in the Hainan Island, South China Block: Implications for Neo-Tethyan Subduction
content: The Tethyan tectonic domain exerted significant impacts on the tectonic evolution of China. However, magmatic‑petrological records of the Neo‑Tethys in southeastern South China are still poorly constrained. To better understand the formation and evolutionary characteristics of the Neo‑Tethyan tectonic domain in South China. Petrography, zircon U‑Pb geochronology, as well as elemental‑isotopic geochemical analyses were carried out on the magmatic rocks from Hainan Island. Geochronological results show that two mafic rock samples yield crystallization ages of 99 ± 1 Ma and 98 ± 1 Ma, respectively, and three granite samples give ages of 97 ± 2 Ma, 98 ± 1 Ma and 102 ± 2 Ma. The mafic samples have SiO₂ contents ranging from 49.98% to 51.26 %, belonging to the calc‑alkaline series. They are enriched in large‑ion lithophile elements, depleted in high‑field‑strength elements, and characterized by enriched light rare‑earth elements. Their εHf(t) values range from −5.26 to −3.19. The granite samples have SiO₂ contents of 73.01 %–76.31 %, and are classified as peraluminous high‑K calc‑alkaline rocks with pronounced negative Nb‑Ta anomalies. Their εHf(t) values vary from −5.47 to −2.84, with two‑stage Hf model ages of 1109–1209 Ma. Synthesis of the above data indicates that the mafic rocks were mainly derived from partial melting of enriched lithospheric mantle metasomatized by subduction‑zone fluids/melts. The granites originated from remelting of Mesoproterozoic crustal materials, with the addition of mantle‑derived materials. Combined with the previously identified Cretaceous EW‑trending subduction zone along the northern margin of the South China Sea, we propose that the subduction of Neo‑Tethyan oceanic crust represents the principal geodynamic mechanism for the extensive Cretaceous magmatism on Hainan Island.
